title: [Fix] Fall back to triton MOE for GPT-OSS on Blackwell with driver >= 595 (#21780)
body:
## Summary
- The `triton_kernels` external package segfaults (SIGSEGV, exit code -11) on B200 (Blackwell) GPUs with NVIDIA driver >= 595.58.03 during MoE forward pass (`matmul_ogs` / `routing` / `topk` kernels)
- This causes `test_gpt_oss_4gpu.py::test_bf16_120b` to consistently fail on `b200-dgx-020-*` CI runners (driver 595.58.03) while passing on `b200-novita-1` (driver 590.48.01) and all H100 runners
- Adds shared `get_nvidia_driver_version_str()` / `get_nvidia_driver_version()` utilities in `common.py` and uses them to fall back to the `triton` MOE backend (instead of `triton_kernel`) when Blackwell + driver >= 595 is detected
- Consolidates duplicated nvidia-smi driver version queries in `check_env.py` and `killall.py` to reuse the new shared utility

title: [ROCm] Eliminate redundant contiguous copy in MLA attention on ROCm MXFP4 (#25463)
body: ## Motivation On the ROCm MXFP4 decode path (`_use_aiter_gfx95` with `w_vc.dtype == torch.uint8`), the `batched_gemm_afp4wfp4_pre_quant` kernel outputs `attn_bmm_output` in `(heads, batch, v_head_dim)` layout. The current code then does: ```python attn_bmm_output = attn_bmm_output.transpose(0, 1).flatten(1, 2) ``` The `.transpose(0, 1)` makes the tensor non-contiguous, so `.flatten(1, 2)` triggers an implicit `.contiguous()` copy — appearing as a `direct_copy_kernel_cuda` (`elementwise_kernel_manual_unroll`) in profiling traces at **~4µs per layer**. With 61 MoE layers this adds up to **~268µs per decode step** of unnecessary data movement. ## Changes Pre-allocate the output buffer in `(batch, heads, v_head_dim)` layout (the target shape) and pass a transposed view `(heads, batch, v_head_dim)` to the GEMM kernel. The aiter `batched_gemm_a16wfp4` Triton kernel already accepts arbitrary output strides via explicit `stride_cb`, `stride_cm`, `stride_cn` parameters, so it writes correctly into the non-contiguous view. After the GEMM, `.flatten(1, 2)` on the already-contiguous `(batch, heads, v_head_dim)` buffer is a zero-cost view — no copy needed. **Scope:** Only affects the `_use_aiter_gfx95 and self.w_vc.dtype == torch.uint8` branch (MXFP4 on MI355X/gfx950). All other backends and platforms are untouched. ## Profiling Evidence **Platform:** MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2, TP=4, Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4, ISL=8192, OSL=1024, CONC=4 Per-layer decode kernel trace (MLA attention section only): ### Before (19 kernels/layer) ``` kn_mla_reduce_v1_ps 10.4µs _batched_gemm_a16wfp4 3.9µs elementwise_manual_unroll 4.4µs ← contiguous copy hgemm_bf16 (o_proj) 9.2µs allreduce_fusion 7.8µs ``` ### After (18 kernels/layer) ``` kn_mla_reduce_v1_ps 10.2µs _batched_gemm_a16wfp4 4.2µs hgemm_bf16 (o_proj) 11.5µs ← direct, no copy allreduce_fusion 6.5µs ``` The `elementwise_kernel_manual_unroll` between `batched_gemm` and `hgemm_bf16` is eliminated. before: after PR: ## Accuracy Verification GSM8K accuracy via `lm_eval` (250 problems, 5-shot, `openai-completions` backend): | Metric | Value | Threshold | |---|---|---| | `exact_match,flexible-extract` | **0.932** | ≥ …[truncated]

title: [DCP]Localize HiCache DCP indices once per transfer, not per layer (#34889)
body: ## Motivation Under DCP, `MLATokenToKVPoolHost.load_to_device_per_layer()` translated the widened logical slots into this rank's physical rows on every call: ```python host_indices = self.dcp_kernel_indices(host_indices) device_indices = self.dcp_kernel_indices(device_indices) ``` The result is layer-independent, but the load loop calls the method once per layer. The cost is worse than the launch count suggests. `indices[indices % dcp_size == dcp_rank]` is boolean-mask indexing, which goes through `nonzero` — and `nonzero` must read the selected count back to the host to size its output. That is a **device→host sync**, and it runs inside `with device_module.stream(self.load_stream)`, so each layer's translation blocks on the previous layer's transfer kernel. The loop serialises. `start_loading()` runs on the scheduler thread (`get_new_batch_prefill` → `ready_to_load_host_cache`), so the stall sits directly in front of the forward launch. ## Modifications - `HostKVCache.dcp_localize_indices(host_indices, device_indices)` translates a transfer's index pair once. - `load_to_device_per_layer()` now *takes* this rank's physical rows — the translation is gone from the MLA implementation. This makes explicit the precondition `_backup_from_device_per_layer` already relies on ("Indices arrive already translated…"). - `HiCacheController.start_loading()` localizes once ahead of its layer loop. - `backup_from_device_all_layer()` keeps translating internally — it owns its own layer loop, so it already paid the cost once per write-back. Not touched: the draft, HiSparse, and `HostPoolGroup` load paths. All three are rejected or non-DCP under `_resolve_hicache_dcp_compatibility`, so the translation is the identity there and un-localized indices are already correct. Pools that are not DCP-sharded return the inputs unchanged, so nothing changes unless `--dcp-size > 1`. ## Profiling Before After ## Benchmarking 8×B300, DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat (MLA, 27 layers), `--tp-size 8 --dcp-size 8 --page-size 64 --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 4`, 16384 tokens/rank. title: [DeepSeek v3.2] opt Context Parallelism: support fused moe, multi batch and fp8 kvcache (#13959)
body: ## Motivation The original default token splitting scheme of cp does not support prefill multi-batch. A new token splitting method is introduced to enable multi-batch support, fused MoE compatibility, and FP8 KV-cache support. Compared with the original DeepEP scheme, the combination of the tuned fused MoE backend and the new token splitting method **reduces TTFT by 8.9% (for inputs ≥16K tokens) to 32% (for 1K token inputs)** in 8× H20(141GB). H20-3e fused MoE tuning configurations will be submitted in the next PR. Activate via the `--nsa-prefill-cp-mode round-robin-split` flag (default: `in-seq-split`, which uses the original token splitting scheme). Tokens are evenly distributed with the rank calculated as `token_idx % cp_size`, ensuring balanced computation across all indexers. ## Modifications 1. Support for the new token splitting scheme: compatibility adaptations for `cp_split_and_rebuild_data`, `cp_split_and_rebuild_position`, and `cp_all_gather_rerange_output`. 2. title: [Perf] FlashInfer MLA: remove blocking D2H in spec-decode plan (#27689)
body:
## Motivation

On H200, DeepSeek-R1 with MTP/EAGLE (`--speculative-num-steps 2 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 3`) was **no faster than standard decoding**, which shouldn't happen. nsys showed 3 synchronous device→host copies per attention `plan()` in the target-verify and draft-extend steps. Being blocking, they stall the host thread that launches the next CUDA graph, breaking overlap scheduling — and the stalls negate the speculation benefit.

Root cause: `BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper.plan()` copies `qo_indptr`/`kv_indptr`/`kv_len_arr` to host via blocking `.to("cpu")` when handed GPU tensors. The normal decode path already avoids this via `fast_mla_decode_plan` (it passes pre-computed CPU tensors), but the spec-decode verify and draft-extend paths still used the stock plan.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/flashinfer_mla_backend.py` only:
- Allocate pinned host buffers `fast_plan_{qo_indptr,kv_indptr,kv_len_arr}_cpu` in `__init__` (prefill-capable backends only).
- **Target-verify (cuda graph):** add `fast_mla_prefill_plan` — a sibling of the existing `fast_mla_decode_plan`, analogous to the merged `fast_prefill_plan` in #28854. It hands host-known `qo/kv indptr + lengths` straight to `_cached_module.plan` (no per-replay D2H) and refreshes the cuda-graph buffers, and is installed on the verify wrapper at capture once the real `plan()` has populated `_cached_module`. The verify branch builds the host arrays from `seq_lens_cpu` + the fixed `num_draft_tokens` tree shape and asserts them (fail-fast; the sync-free plan has no device-readback fallback).
- **Eager `DRAFT_EXTEND_V2`** (`init_forward_metadata`) builds the same host arrays and passes them to `plan()` so its `.to("cpu")` no-ops (flashinfer-MLA has no draft-extend cuda graph, so this path is eager).
- `kv_indices` stays on GPU throughout. Decode, normal prefill, and ragged paths are unchanged.

### Note on the `seq_lens_cpu` dependency (re: review)

This feeds `plan()` `seq_lens_cpu`-derived host arrays; it does not *remove* the `seq_lens_cpu` dependency. Fully removing it — as #26824 did for `trtllm_mla` via `needs_cpu_seq_lens=False` — requires **GPU-side** attention planning. FlashInfer-MLA's `plan()` is **host-side** (it reads the indptr/lengths on the CPU to build the tile schedule), so it fundamentally needs the lengths on the host. The merged #28854 takes the same approach (it also `assert`s `seq_lens_cpu is not None` and sets `kv_lens_host = seq_lens_cpu`). The residual per-iteration `seq_lens_cpu` D2H sync is a scheduler-level cost inheren …[truncated]

title: [AMD][DSV4] feat: enable DSpark with fp8 unified_kv on gfx950 (#38901)
body:
## Motivation


Follow-up to [#37413](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37413). Incremental is only 1 commit, 6 files.

In #37413 we added fp8 two-pool unified_kv on gfx950 (`SGLANG_DSV4_UNIFIED_KV_FP8`, 640 B/row, ~1.50× KV capacity) and measured it on MTP. We left DSpark as the next SPD path.

`--speculative-algorithm DSPARK` plus the env builds a second `DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool` for the draft worker. That constructor used process-wide `is_unified_kv_fp8()`, and CUDA-graph capture died on `kv.dtype == unified_kv.dtype`. Same env, DSpark now comes up. Target decode / prefill / `target_verify` stay on the two-pool. MTP is unchanged.

## Modifications


AMD / HIP `unified_kv_triton` only. Default off. No change to `is_unified_kv_fp8()`, `DSparkAttention`, or the scatter kernel.

- **DSpark under the fp8 env.** `_build_dsv4_kv_pool` selects the layout per pool: `unified_fp8=is_unified_kv_fp8() and not (is_draft_worker and spec_algorithm.is_dspark())`. Target follows the env (640 B two-pool). EAGLE/MTP draft still follows the env.
- **Sizing.** With DSpark+fp8, `_fixed_swa_bytes` budgets the target fp8 ring plus the draft SWA ring at 1024 B/row (one layer for shipped drafts), not `(T+1)/T * 640`. `bytes_per_full_token` still multiplies `(T+1)/T` — conservative; DSpark draft has no C4/C128. MTP inflation is the same as #37413.

## What this buys: KV capacity
Same CLI pair, Flash-DSpark, TP=8 DP=8 + dp-attention, gfx950. Differs only in `SGLANG_DSV4_UNIFIED_KV_FP8`. Same 1.50× as #37413, on DSpark.

body:
## Motivation

EAGLE v1 is deprecated — all speculative workers are v2. This removes the v1 `ForwardMode.DRAFT_EXTEND` mode and every code path keyed on it. `ForwardMode.DRAFT_EXTEND_V2` is untouched and will be renamed to `DRAFT_EXTEND` in a follow-up PR.

## Commits

1. **Rename `is_draft_extend(include_v2=True)` → `is_draft_extend_v2()`** (mechanical, behavior-identical). `is_draft_extend(include_v2=True)` returned `self == DRAFT_EXTEND or self == DRAFT_EXTEND_V2`, but v1 `DRAFT_EXTEND` is never produced by any live path, so it already equaled `is_draft_extend_v2()`. Reproducible regex transform is in the commit message.
2. **Remove the v1 `DRAFT_EXTEND` mode.**

title: Fix the chunked-prefix-cache gate writing config the backends never read (#33168)
body:
## Motivation

The load-time chunked-prefix gate (`maybe_disable_chunked_prefix_cache`) still writes its `ServerArgs` instance, but every reader has moved to the published config: the attention backends assert / branch on `get_schedule().disable_chunked_prefix_cache` when they initialize. The flip never reaches them, so an MLA model on a backend outside `CHUNKED_PREFIX_CACHE_SUPPORTED_ATTENTION_BACKENDS` keeps chunked prefix enabled instead of being gated off.

## Modifications

- `misc_utils.maybe_disable_chunked_prefix_cache`: the gate writes through `get_context().override` (lands on the published bags) and its own pre/post checks read the bag.
- `prefill_cuda_graph_runner`: the `_capture_chunked_prefix` flag reads the bag the gate writes, not the runner's `ServerArgs` copy.
- New regression test pins the three contracts: the gate lands on the bag, the pristine `ServerArgs` instance stays untouched, and the draft-worker guard never writes.
- `ServerArgs.override` call-site ratchet drops 39 -> 38.

title: [V1] Optimize the CPU overheads in FlashAttention custom op (#10733)
body:
With piece-wise CUDA graphs, we have to make sure that the attention custom op causes minimal CPU overheads. This PR made a few changes to optimize the CPU overheads in the FlashAttention custom op:
1. ~~We directly use `torch.ops.vllm_flash_attn_c.varlen_fwd` rather than `flash_attn_varlen_func`, since `FlashAttnFunc` which inherits `torch.autograd.Function` causes unnecessary overheads.~~
2. We move the reshapes and shape check logics to outside of the custom op, so that they can be done at the CUDA graph capture time.

Results of `python benchmarks/benchmark_latency.py` (opt-125m) on a single H100 GPU:
* V1 main: 227 ms
* V1 this PR: 192 ms
* V0 + 8-step: 130 ms

Next step: further reduce the unnecessary CPU ops inside the FlashAttention op.

title: [Kimi-K3] support DCP partial prefix cache hit (#50493)
body:
Builds on the Kimi-K3 DCP support from #50484.

* Enables hash-aligned partial-prefix reuse under DCP for FullAttention plus aligned Mamba while preserving sharded-attention and replicated-Mamba correctness.
* Fixes MRV2 block-table geometry. MRV2 previously divided every cache group's block-table width by DCP size—correct for attention, but wrong for replicated Mamba. For a 1M context, DCP8, and 16-token Mamba blocks, it allocated 8,192 entries instead of 65,536, potentially causing metadata corruption and CUDA illegal-address failures. The fix uses cache-type-specific sizing and adds a bounds check.

Validation:

* focused functional and MRV2 tests: 49 passed;
* DCP MLA non-virtual-block-aligned metadata test: passed;
* pre-commit lint, format, type, SPDX, and policy hooks: passed.

title: [Bugfix] Fix handling 5D KV cache in kv_postprocess_layout_on_receive (#47791)
body:
## PR Purpose

Fixes `IndexError` in `kv_postprocess_layout_on_receive()` for 5D blocks-first KV caches.

`kv_postprocess_layout_on_receive()` (added in #30275) permutes a received KV cache from HND to NHD layout. It assumes the cache is 4D. But since #42095 is recently merged, non-MLA backends allocate a 5D cache `(num_blocks, 2, block_size, H, D)`. This causes the following error:

```bash
IndexError: index_copy_(): Source dimensionality (4), destination dimensionality (5)
```
(This was also flagged as future work in #37943)

### Fix
Use a 5D-aware `inv_order` when the cache is 5D (while 4D path remains unchanged)

## Test Plan
Quick test with:
```bash
DECODER_KV_LAYOUT=NHD DECODER_ATTENTION_BACKEND=TRITON_ATTN \
bash tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/run_accuracy_test.sh
```

## Test Result
Before: `IndexError`
After: **pass**

cc @xuechendi @NickLucche @yzong-rh
